newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher, unlinked bonds stable.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher, unlinked bonds stable.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Monday with unlinked bonds breaking a string of declines as yields reached attractive levels, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.09 pct to 107.24
Volume including Makams was 195 million shekels, with turnover in dollar-linked bonds at a high 48 million shekels.

"The unlinked market, which had suffered on the strengthening of the dollar, finally stabilised today and even showed a reversal of trend despite its being the end of the month when you generally have surplus supplies of these bonds," said Tiki Hadad of IBI Investment House.
Unlinked bonds had been falling in previous sessions as a soaring dollar boosted fears of a rise in inflation.
"The market expects this rise (in the dollar) to be reflected in the coming consumer price indices," said a trader.

Hadad said the turnaround in unlinked bonds did not reflect a re-assessment of the inflationary outlook but the yield level. "Yields of the unlinked bonds are an attractive 13.2 percent," she said Hadad.

The shekel has plunged some five percent in the last two days, reaching 3.587 on the dollar on Monday, after the Israeli cabinet approved exchange rate reforms that widened the diagonal band in which the currency may trade.

"Demand was up again for CPI-linked short bonds on fears of a higher inflation. CPI-linked long bonds fell slightly. The yield curve is now flat, with yields of short and long bonds around 4.15-4.20 percent," Hadad said.

Prices of dollar-linked bonds closed slightly higher. Hadad said that as the dollar weakened in early morning trading, dollar-linked bonds had been in surplus. But as the U.S. currency rebounded, demand for dollar bonds revived.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5870 shekels against 3.5920 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
